Measured 2026-08-22 over normalized_text (362,717 chars, 6,188 lines): 392 lines are nothing but furniture -- '' 75x, '' 73x, '' 72x, '
' 72x, '' 27x, and 73 ''/'' column-marker lines whose text differs per table because the column padding does. That last group is why the rule is a regex over the whole stripped line rather than a set of literals. Bands rather than exact counts, for the reason given in boilerplate-chrome-detected's provenance. ge-1994 is also the reason edgar_chrome is resolved BEFORE running_head: '' here occurs 75x at CV 0.40, spread 0.99, so it clears the running_head gates too. Resolution order (ADR-026 §b) gives it the more specific kind and guarantees exactly one span per line. The four max-0 checks are the near-miss direction for this era. 'Item 1. Business' is the real body heading and must never be furniture. 'GECS' (19x) and 'GE' (18x) are the shortest repeated lines in the document -- a length-based rule would have taken both. The 70-dash rule line occurs 37x at CV 0.82, spread 0.66: it is arguably chrome and is deliberately NOT detected (ADR-026 §f1), and this check pins that as a decision rather than leaving it to drift silently into scope later. offsets_invariant_under_exclusion carries the txt half of the INV-S2 acceptance criterion; boilerplate-offsets-invariant carries the HTML half in the invariant suite. Both eras are covered because txt is the only era where normalization does not rewrite the body, so it is the era where an offset bug would look different.
